transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Chen, thank you for coming in. I wanted to talk to you about your biopsy results.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: The cancer. Is it bad?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Well, there have been some issues with the processing. There was some confusion with how the samples were handled.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Confusion? I do not understand.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is just a system problem. Sometimes things do not go quite right in the lab.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So I have the cancer? I am very scared.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am sorry for any confusion this has caused, but we were really busy last week and some things got mixed up.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I cannot sleep. My daughter says we must start the medicine.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Let's just focus on the details here. The problem is that the pathology reports were not aligned.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't know these words. What is pathology?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is just the lab. Look, we need to move through this because I have to go to another clinic in ten minutes.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But my life... if I am sick, what do I do?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. But as I said, there was a mix-up.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A mix-up? Who is sick?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was an issue with the labeling.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are not telling me. Do I have the cancer or not?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are looking into it. I can't say for sure right now because the lab is reviewing the files.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You told me last week it was cancer. You said it was stage three.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is why I am here. There were inconsistencies in the documentation.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am very confused. Why is this happening?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Like I said, it's a system error.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel like I am dreaming. This is too much.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will get it sorted. We just need to wait for the new reports.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When? When do I know?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Sometime soon. Maybe a few days.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will you call me?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll have someone send an email or maybe a letter.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I do not check email. I don't have a computer.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Then we will just see what happens. We'll keep you posted.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But the medicine... the chemotherapy...

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We aren't doing that yet. We have to wait.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am so worried. My heart is beating very fast.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's okay. Just try to relax. Now, as I mentioned, I really have to head out.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't understand what happened to my biopsy.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was just some confusion in the lab.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Did they lose it?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, there was just an issue with the files.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So I am not sick?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can't give you a definitive answer until the lab clears it up.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't know what to tell my family.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Just tell them we are double checking.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why did you tell me I had cancer first?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Because the first report said so, but then we found the inconsistency.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I cannot believe this.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will reach out when we have more.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When exactly?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Probably by next week.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Please tell me the truth.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am telling you there was a problem with the system.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want to know if I am dying.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We just need to wait for the email.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I told you I have no email.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Right. Then we'll see. I have to go now.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('move through this because I have to go', 'I really have to head out', 'I have to go now').

E.justification: Resident uses only platitudes and vague terms ('system problem', 'confusion', 'mix-up') without explicitly naming the error.

A.justification: Responsibility is consistently deflected to 'the system', 'the lab', and 'the files' despite a brief apology for confusion.

R.justification: Patient's emotional bids ('I am very scared', 'my heart is beating very fast') are consistently met with factual redirection or dismissive phrases.

T.justification: The plan consists of placeholders and vague timelines ('Sometime soon', 'Maybe a few days', 'we'll see what happens').
